messages:
Noah: hey all, Noah here (first day!). Quick question: where do I drop issues for device setup, flaky infra, product feedback, and UX asks? Also a bunch of bots DM'ed me after I accepted invites  any recommended mute patterns so I don't miss pages?

Ravi: welcome Noah! short breakdown: device/setup -> #help (include screenshot + OS), flaky infra -> #incidents if it impacts users, otherwise #eng-infra or #build-failures, product feedback -> #product-feedback, UX/design -> #design. If it's squad-specific, post in the squad channel (e.g., #s-recommender).

Noah: thanks. for noisy CI/build bots, is muting the channel enough or do we have finer controls?

Elena: muting channels hides messages but not app mentions. For finer control go to the app in "Apps" (top-left) -> find the bot -> uncheck "Send me messages" or adjust notifications. We usually mute CI channels and rely on the deploy bot to page when something is critical.

support-bot: Hello Noah! To finish onboarding run:

```
$ rwi-setup init --auto
$ rwi-auth grant
```

Reply "done" when complete.

Noah: ran it, hit a permission denied on /var/run/docker.sock. Who should I ping?

Ravi: open a short post in #help and tag @infra-team. Include the error line and your hostname. That'll get a faster response than DMs.

Noah: good call. one more: when is it ok to use @channel vs @here vs @team? I'm worried about disturbing others across timezones.

Elena: rules we follow: @channel = rare, big announcements only (team-wide or org-wide). @here = okay for time-sensitive asks for people currently active in the channel (use sparingly). @team (custom user groups) = only after confirming with the team's manager. If unsure, DM a lead or post in a thread and ask for an async reply.

Noah: got it. what about posting intros? in #introductions or just in my squad?

Ravi: do both: 1) Short intro in #introductions (name, role, timezone, one fun fact). 2) In your squad channel, say what you'll own in the next week. People appreciate linking an RFC or initial ticket if you have it.

Elena: small etiquette tips: 1) use threads for follow-ups, 2) use :eyes: or :thumbsup: reactions for quick ACKs instead of full replies, 3) prefix channel threads with [FYI]/[Help]/[Decision] if it's a longer post so it reads better in search.

Noah: awesome, thanks. I'll mute the noisy CI channel, add @oncall to my notification keywords, and post intros in both places. appreciate the help! :grinning:
